correctness.rationale: Edge increments identify \(\mathcal F(C_n)\) isometrically with \(\ell_1^n/\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\), whose dual is the zero-sum section of the \(\ell_\infty^n\) cube. The primal extreme points are \(\pm q(e_i)\). For even \(n\), every norming balanced-sign dual extreme can be globally reversed to have the prescribed coordinate \(+1\), forcing numerical radius to equal operator norm. For odd \(n\), dual extremes have one zero coordinate; median centering gives the lower bound \((n-2)/(n-1)\), and the only exceptional norming-coordinate case loses at most the smallest of the \(n-1\) nonzero coordinates. The cyclic-shift witness has norm one, satisfies the sole quotient compatibility relation, and attains equality. The checker confirms small cases but the all-\(n\) conclusion is proved symbolically.

final_claim: For every real unit-edge cycle \(C_n\) with \(n\ge6\), \(n(\mathcal F(C_n))=1\) when \(n\) is even and \(n(\mathcal F(C_n))=(n-2)/(n-1)\) when \(n\) is odd.
limitations: Real scalars and unit-edge shortest-path cycles only.
